chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Maqarri narrated to us, saying: Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Maqarri al-Jarjani narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mawsili in Baghdad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Asim al-Tarifi narrated to us, saying: Abu Zayd 'Ayash ibn Yazid ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kahhal, the servant of Zayd ibn Ali, narrated to us, saying: My father, Yazid ibn al-Hasan, narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) narrated to me, saying: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'The Day when Allah will gather the Messengers and say: What were you responded with? They will say: We have no knowledge.' He said: They will say: We have no knowledge of other than You. He said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: The Qur'an, all of it, is reproach, and its internal meaning is an approximation.

key_terms.يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ الرُّسُلَ: The Day when Allah gathers the Messengers

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the meaning of 'We have no knowledge' in Surah Al-Ma'idah and the dual nature of the Qur'an?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the Messengers' declaration of 'no knowledge' in Quran 5:109 signifies their exclusive reliance on divine knowledge, distinguishing them from those who claim independent insight. He further introduces the concept of *zahir* and *batin* in the Quran, explaining that the text serves as a rebuke (*taqree'*) for the heedless, while its inner essence acts as a means of spiritual approach (*taqrīb*) to God, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the layered nature of revelation.
